source: Quiz 3 - Sessions 1-4: Model Size, Thinking, and Skills
question: Which part of a skill stays loaded in an agent's context even when the skill is not currently being used?

options.feedback: The name and description are what let the model recognize a matching request before anything else about the skill has loaded, so those two pieces stay resident even when the skill is idle.

options.text: The full body of its instructions
options.feedback: The instruction body is exactly the part that loads only on demand, once the skill is actually triggered by a matching request. Keeping it resident all the time is what the on-demand design avoids.

options.text: Any scripts it bundles, such as a frame-extraction script
options.feedback: Scripts are among the heaviest parts of a skill, which is why they load only when the skill actually runs, not just because the skill exists in the library.

options.text: Its reference files and output-format examples
options.feedback: Reference files and output-format examples are useful once the skill is in use, but loading them permanently for every skill in a library would recreate the exact bloat the on-demand pattern is built to prevent.
